topics.name: Biodiversity
concepts: Two-kingdom: Linnaeus; five-kingdom: Whittaker (1969); three domains (Archaea, Bacteria, Eukarya): Carl Woese
Hierarchy: Kingdom → Division → Class → Order → Family → Genus → Species [repeat]
Archaebacteria: no peptidoglycan wall, ether-linked membrane lipids; methanogens, halophiles, thermoacidophiles [repeat]
Viruses: nucleic acid + capsid; TMV ssRNA, T4 phage dsDNA; viroid = naked RNA; Beijerinck: contagium vivum fluidum
Cyanobacteria: heterocysts fix N₂; phycobilins shared with red algae; store cyanophycean starch [repeat]
Rhizopus = black bread mould; Mucor: zygospores; yeast (Ascomycetes) buds and ferments sugar to ethanol + CO₂ [repeat]
Lichen = alga + fungus; crustose, foliose, fruticose (Usnea); cyphellae for gas exchange; SO₂ indicators [repeat]
Algae stores: green starch, brown laminarin/mannitol, red floridean starch; agar from Gelidium, algin from brown algae
Spirogyra: spiral ribbon chloroplast, scalariform/lateral conjugation, zygospore is the only diploid stage
Bryophytes: gametophyte dominant, sporophyte dependent; Marchantia gemmae; Anthoceros basal meristem [repeat]
Dryopteris: dictyostele rhizome, reniform indusium, heart-shaped bisexual haploid prothallus [repeat]
Pinus: monoecious, winged pollen, haploid endosperm; chilgoza from Pinus gerardiana; P. roxburghii needles in 3s [repeat]
Stem modifications: ginger rhizome, potato tuber, banana sucker; stilt roots from lower nodes of maize [repeat]
Families: Brassicaceae siliqua + replum, tetradynamous; Fabaceae vexillary, diadelphous; Solanaceae oblique ovary; Liliaceae P3+3 A3+3 G(3) [repeat]
Spirogyra/Mucor zygospore undergoes meiosis; red algae grow deepest; iodine from kelps; fern antherozoids multiflagellate [repeat]
Medicinal: Neem azadirachtin, Sarpagandha reserpine (hypertension), Yarsagumba fungus on caterpillar, Tulsi cough, Ginger nausea

topics.name: Ecology & Vegetation
concepts: Pond: phytoplankton producers; littoral zone rooted plants; energy pyramid always upright; 10% law
Interactions: mutualism (+,+), commensalism (+,0), amensalism (−,0), parasitism (+,−); Cuscuta is a parasite
Interlinked food chains form a food web [repeat]
Nitrogen cycle: Rhizobium fixes, Nitrosomonas NH₃→NO₂⁻, Nitrobacter NO₂⁻→NO₃⁻, Pseudomonas denitrifies
CO₂ is the main anthropogenic greenhouse gas; methane from paddy fields and cattle
Acid rain: SO₂ and NOₓ; ozone in stratosphere measured in Dobson units; CFC chlorine destroys ozone
Forest zones of Nepal: Sal in Terai/Siwalik (tropical); Schima–Castanopsis and chir pine subtropical [repeat]
Invasive aliens in Nepal: Mikania micrantha, Lantana, Parthenium, water hyacinth
Succession: pioneer → seral stages → climax; abandoned field = secondary succession [repeat]
Hydrosere: phytoplankton → submerged → floating → reed-swamp → sedge-meadow → woodland → forest [repeat]
Xerosere pioneer: crustose lichens; xerophytes have sunken stomata; hydrophytes have aerenchyma
Heliophytes are sun-loving, sciophytes shade-loving [repeat]
Obligate mutualism (+,+); Gause competitive exclusion; benthos on bottom; velamen in epiphytes; eutrophication lowers dissolved O₂
Tropical rainforests hold maximum species diversity [repeat]

topics.name: Plant Anatomy
concepts: Meristems: apical (length), intercalary (grass internode base), lateral (girth)
Collenchyma: living, corner thickening of cellulose/pectin; sclerenchyma: dead, lignified fibres and sclereids
Xylem parenchyma is the only living xylem element; companion cells occur only in angiosperms
Vessels absent in gymnosperms (except Gnetales); tracheids conduct water there
Bundles: radial (roots), conjoint collateral open (dicot stem), closed (monocot stem) [repeat]
Bicollateral: Cucurbita; amphicribral (phloem around xylem): ferns; amphivasal: Dracaena [repeat]
Monocot stem: scattered bundles = atactostele; lysigenous water cavity; dicot stem eustele [repeat]
Roots: exarch xylem; dicot root di- to tetrarch, monocot root polyarch with large pith
Casparian strips in endodermis; lateral roots arise endogenously from pericycle
Dicot leaf dorsiventral (palisade + spongy); grass leaf isobilateral with bulliform cells
Grass guard cells dumb-bell shaped; Kranz anatomy in C₄ leaves
Monocots cannot be grafted: no cambium [repeat]; old sieve plates sealed by callose; cork walls suberised; companion cells living

topics.name: Applied Botany
concepts: Totipotency: a single cell can form a whole plant; Haberlandt = father of tissue culture
Explant surface sterilised with sodium hypochlorite/HgCl₂/ethanol; medium autoclaved at 121 °C, 15 psi [repeat]
High cytokinin: shoots; high auxin: roots; balance: callus
Meristem culture gives virus-free plants; anther culture gives haploids; protoplast fusion gives somatic hybrids (pomato)
Cryopreservation of germplasm in liquid nitrogen at −196 °C [repeat]
Restriction enzymes cut (EcoRI GAATTC), DNA ligase joins; Ti plasmid of Agrobacterium tumefaciens is a vector [repeat]
PCR uses Taq polymerase; DNA moves to the anode in gel electrophoresis
Bt cotton: cry gene of Bacillus thuringiensis; Golden rice: β-carotene [repeat]
Biofertilizers: Rhizobium, Azotobacter, Azolla–Anabaena, mycorrhiza; green manure: Sesbania, sunn hemp
Heterosis = hybrid vigour; Norman Borlaug led the Green Revolution with semi-dwarf wheat
Bio-engineering: live plants (grasses, bamboo, shrubs) stabilise slopes and control erosion
Food security: all people, at all times, access to sufficient, safe, nutritious food; aflatoxin from Aspergillus flavus

questions.q: The five-kingdom classification was proposed by
questions.x: Whittaker (1969): Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, Animalia.
questions.trap: Woese gave the three-domain system.

questions.q: An infectious agent made only of a small, naked circular RNA without a protein coat is a
questions.x: Viroids (Diener, 1971) cause plant diseases such as potato spindle tuber; they lack a capsid.
questions.trap: Prions are infectious proteins with no nucleic acid.

questions.q: The genetic material of tobacco mosaic virus (TMV) is
questions.x: TMV is a rod-shaped plant virus with ssRNA inside a protein coat.

questions.q: In Nostoc and Anabaena, nitrogen fixation takes place in
questions.x: Heterocysts are thick-walled cells lacking PS II, so nitrogenase is protected from O₂.
questions.trap: Akinetes are resting spores, not N₂-fixing cells.

questions.q: Gram-positive bacteria retain the crystal violet stain because they have
questions.x: The thick peptidoglycan layer traps the crystal violet–iodine complex during alcohol wash.
questions.trap: Outer LPS membrane belongs to Gram-negative bacteria.

questions.q: Transfer of bacterial DNA from one bacterium to another through a bacteriophage is called
questions.x: In transduction a phage carries host DNA to a new bacterium.
questions.trap: Transformation is uptake of free DNA (Griffith).

questions.q: Lichens are good indicators of air pollution by
questions.x: Lichens are highly sensitive to SO₂ and disappear from polluted areas.

questions.q: Mycorrhizal fungi mainly benefit the host plant by increasing absorption of
questions.x: Fungal hyphae extend the root's absorbing surface and especially increase phosphate uptake.

questions.q: Scalariform (ladder-like) conjugation is characteristic of
questions.x: Two Spirogyra filaments join by conjugation tubes, appearing like a ladder.

questions.q: The brown colour of Phaeophyceae (brown algae) is due to
questions.x: Fucoxanthin, a xanthophyll, masks chlorophyll in brown algae.
questions.trap: Phycoerythrin gives the red colour of red algae.

questions.q: The main plant body of a moss (e.g. Funaria) is
questions.x: In bryophytes the gametophyte (n) is dominant; the sporophyte grows on it.
questions.trap: Pteridophytes have a dominant sporophyte, not bryophytes.

questions.q: Heterospory is found in
questions.x: Selaginella produces microspores and megaspores; the others are homosporous.
questions.trap: Lycopodium is related to Selaginella but is homosporous.

questions.q: The endosperm of a gymnosperm such as Pinus is
questions.x: Gymnosperm endosperm is female gametophyte tissue (n); there is no double fertilization.
questions.trap: Triploid is the angiosperm endosperm.

questions.q: Vexillary aestivation is characteristic of the family
questions.x: Pea flowers have a large standard overlapping two wings, which overlap the keel.

questions.q: Tetradynamous stamens are found in
questions.x: Brassicaceae (mustard) has 6 stamens: 4 long inner and 2 short outer.

questions.q: A bicarpellary, obliquely placed ovary with swollen axile placentae is a feature of
questions.x: Solanaceae (potato, tomato, Datura) has an oblique bilocular ovary with swollen placentae.
questions.trap: Fabaceae has a monocarpellary ovary with marginal placentation.

questions.q: Marginal placentation is found in
questions.x: Monocarpellary pea ovary bears ovules along the ventral suture (margin).
questions.trap: Mustard is parietal; China rose axile; Dianthus free central.

questions.q: The edible part of mango is the
questions.x: Mango is a drupe; its fleshy, juicy mesocarp is eaten.
questions.trap: Endosperm is the edible part of coconut.

questions.q: Casparian strips are present in the root
questions.x: Suberin bands on radial and inner tangential walls of endodermis block apoplastic flow.
questions.trap: Pericycle lies just inside endodermis and is a common confusion.
questions.s: T.S. of monocot and dicot root

questions.q: Scattered, closed vascular bundles without cambium are characteristic of
questions.x: Monocot stems (e.g. maize) have many scattered closed bundles in ground tissue.
questions.trap: Roots have radial bundles, not scattered ones.
questions.s: Types of vascular bundles; monocot stem

questions.q: Compared with autumn wood, spring wood has
questions.x: In spring cambium is very active, forming large, thin-walled vessels; the wood is light and less dense.
questions.trap: Narrow, dense vessels describe autumn (late) wood.

questions.q: Duramen is another name for
questions.x: Duramen (heartwood) is the dark, non-conducting central wood; sapwood is alburnum.
questions.trap: Sapwood (alburnum) is the outer, conducting wood.

questions.q: Periderm consists of
questions.x: Cork cambium (phellogen) forms cork (phellem) outside and phelloderm inside; together they are periderm.

questions.q: The Ti plasmid used as a vector for plant genetic engineering is obtained from
questions.x: Ti (tumour-inducing) plasmid of A. tumefaciens causes crown gall; disarmed forms transfer genes into plants.
questions.trap: A. rhizogenes carries the Ri plasmid, not Ti.

questions.q: The recognition sequence of the restriction enzyme EcoRI is
questions.x: EcoRI cuts G↓AATTC, leaving sticky ends; GGATCC is BamHI, AAGCTT is HindIII.

questions.q: In plant tissue culture, a high cytokinin to auxin ratio in the medium promotes
questions.x: Skoog and Miller: high cytokinin favours shoots, high auxin favours roots, balanced gives callus.
questions.trap: Root formation needs a high auxin ratio.

questions.q: Virus-free plants are obtained by culturing
questions.x: Viruses rarely reach the rapidly dividing apical meristem, which lacks vascular connection.

questions.q: Which ecological pyramid is always upright?
questions.x: Energy decreases at every trophic level, so the energy pyramid can never be inverted.
questions.trap: Pyramid of biomass is inverted in a pond.

questions.q: Producers in an ecosystem fix 10,000 J of energy. By the 10% law, the energy available to tertiary consumers is
questions.x: 10,000 → 1000 (primary) → 100 (secondary) → 10 J (tertiary).
questions.trap: 100 J stops at secondary consumers.

questions.q: The pioneer community of a xerosere on bare rock is
questions.x: Crustose lichens secrete acids that weather rock and start soil formation.
questions.trap: Phytoplankton are pioneers of a hydrosere.

questions.q: A high biochemical oxygen demand (BOD) of a water body indicates
questions.x: Much organic matter means microbes consume more O₂ to decompose it, raising BOD.

questions.q: In a food chain contaminated with DDT, the highest concentration of DDT is found in
o: Top carnivores such as fish-eating birds
questions.x: DDT is not metabolised or excreted, so it accumulates and magnifies at each trophic level (biomagnification).

questions.q: Which is an example of in-situ conservation?
questions.x: In-situ protects species in their natural habitat; the others are ex-situ.

questions.q: Binomial nomenclature was introduced by
questions.x: Linnaeus (Species Plantarum, 1753) gave each species a two-part Latin name: genus + specific epithet.
questions.trap: Whittaker gave five kingdoms, not binomials.

questions.q: The three-domain system of classification was proposed by
questions.x: Woese (1990) used rRNA sequences to divide life into Archaea, Bacteria and Eukarya.
questions.trap: Whittaker proposed five kingdoms.

questions.q: Which sequence of taxonomic categories is in correct descending order?
questions.x: Kingdom, Division (Phylum), Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species: each rank contains the ones below it.
questions.trap: Swapping order and family is the usual slip.

questions.q: The basic unit of classification is
questions.x: Species is the lowest obligate rank: a group of similar individuals that can interbreed to give fertile offspring.
questions.trap: Genus is the next higher rank, not the basic unit.

questions.q: In Linnaeus's two-kingdom classification, bacteria and fungi were placed in
questions.x: The two-kingdom system grouped every organism with a cell wall and no locomotion under Plantae, including bacteria and fungi.
questions.trap: Monera and Protista came later (Whittaker, Haeckel).

questions.q: Archaebacteria differ from eubacteria in having
questions.x: Archaebacterial walls lack peptidoglycan (muramic acid) and their membranes have branched, ether-linked lipids, letting them survive extreme habitats.
questions.trap: Peptidoglycan is the eubacterial wall polymer.

questions.q: Methanogens that produce methane in the guts of cattle and in marshes belong to
questions.x: Methanogens such as Methanobacterium are archaebacteria; they are used in biogas plants.

questions.q: Comma-shaped bacteria are called
questions.x: Vibrio (e.g. Vibrio cholerae) is curved like a comma; bacillus is rod, coccus round, spirillum spiral.
questions.trap: Spirillum is the long spiral form.

questions.q: Nitrosomonas obtains energy by oxidising ammonia. Its mode of nutrition is
questions.x: Chemoautotrophs fix CO₂ using energy released by oxidising inorganic substances such as NH₃, H₂S or Fe²⁺.
questions.trap: Photoautotrophs use light, not chemical oxidation.

questions.q: In the bacterial growth curve, cells divide at the maximum constant rate during the
questions.x: In log phase numbers double every generation; lag is adjustment, stationary is growth = death, decline is net death.
questions.trap: Lag phase comes first but has little division.

questions.q: A bacterium divides by binary fission every 20 minutes. Starting with one cell, how many cells are present after 2 hours?
questions.x: 2 h = 120 min = 6 generations; 2⁶ = 64 cells.
questions.trap: 12 adds instead of doubling; 32 counts only 5 generations.

questions.q: The smallest free-living organisms, which lack a cell wall, are
questions.x: Mycoplasma (PPLO) has no cell wall, so it is pleomorphic and resistant to penicillin.
questions.trap: Viroids are smaller but are not cells.

questions.q: A pigment group present in both red algae and blue-green algae is
questions.x: Phycocyanin and phycoerythrin (phycobilins) occur in cyanobacteria and Rhodophyceae.
questions.trap: Fucoxanthin is the brown algal pigment.

questions.q: The reserve food of blue-green algae is
questions.x: Cyanobacteria store glycogen-like cyanophycean starch; floridean starch is red algal, laminarin brown algal.
questions.trap: Floridean starch belongs to red algae.

questions.q: Viruses are called obligate intracellular parasites because they
o: Multiply only inside living host cells
questions.x: Viruses have no metabolic machinery; they use the host's ribosomes and enzymes to replicate.

questions.q: The protein coat that surrounds the nucleic acid of a virus is the
questions.x: The capsid is built of protein subunits called capsomeres; some viruses add a lipid envelope outside it.
questions.trap: Envelope is an extra lipid layer, not the protein coat.

questions.q: The genetic material of bacteriophage T4 is
questions.x: T-even phages that infect E. coli carry linear dsDNA inside a polyhedral head.
questions.trap: ssRNA is the TMV answer.

questions.q: The term 'contagium vivum fluidum' (infectious living fluid) for the virus was used by
questions.x: Ivanowsky (1892) showed TMV passes bacterial filters; Beijerinck (1898) called it contagium vivum fluidum; Stanley crystallised it (1935).
questions.trap: Ivanowsky discovered the filterable agent but did not coin this term.

questions.q: The common black bread mould is
questions.x: Rhizopus stolonifer grows on stale bread with black sporangia on stolons and rhizoids.
questions.trap: Penicillium is the blue-green mould.

questions.q: Sexual reproduction in Mucor produces
questions.x: Two compatible gametangia fuse (gametangial copulation) to form a thick-walled zygospore; Mucor is a phycomycete.
questions.trap: Conidia are asexual spores.

questions.q: The common method of asexual reproduction in yeast (Saccharomyces) is
questions.x: A small outgrowth (bud) forms on the parent cell, receives a daughter nucleus and separates, sometimes forming pseudomycelium.

questions.q: Yeast belongs to the class
questions.x: Yeast forms ascospores inside an ascus during sexual reproduction, so it is an ascomycete (sac fungus).
questions.trap: Its unicellular body makes students guess Phycomycetes.

questions.q: Production of bread and beer depends on yeast because it
o: Ferments sugar to ethanol and carbon dioxide
questions.x: Zymase of yeast converts glucose to C₂H₅OH + CO₂; alcohol gives beverages, CO₂ makes dough rise.
questions.trap: Lactic acid comes from Lactobacillus.

questions.q: Fungi in which no sexual stage is known are placed in
questions.x: Deuteromycetes (fungi imperfecti) reproduce only by conidia; e.g. Alternaria, Colletotrichum.

questions.q: Spores borne externally on club-shaped basidia are characteristic of
questions.x: Mushrooms, rusts and smuts bear four basidiospores exogenously on each basidium.
questions.trap: Ascomycetes produce spores inside a sac (endogenous).

questions.q: The cell wall of most true fungi, such as Agaricus, is made mainly of
questions.x: Fungal walls are chitin (a nitrogen-containing polysaccharide), the same polymer as insect exoskeletons.
questions.trap: Cellulose is the green plant wall.

questions.q: Penicillin, the first antibiotic, was discovered by Alexander Fleming from
questions.x: Fleming (1928) saw P. notatum inhibit Staphylococcus colonies.
questions.trap: Streptomyces griseus gives streptomycin.

questions.q: A lichen is a symbiotic association between
o: A fungus and a higher plant root
A bacterium and a legume root
questions.x: The alga (phycobiont) photosynthesises; the fungus (mycobiont) gives shelter, water and minerals.
questions.trap: Fungus + root is mycorrhiza.

questions.q: Small pores on the lower surface of some foliose lichens that help in gaseous exchange are
questions.x: Cyphellae (e.g. in Sticta) are breathing pores; soredia and isidia are vegetative propagules; rhizinae anchor.
questions.trap: Soredia are propagules, not pores.

questions.q: Usnea, with an erect or hanging, branched shrub-like thallus, is a
questions.x: Fruticose lichens are shrubby and attached at one point; crustose are crust-like, foliose are leaf-like.
questions.trap: Foliose lichens are flat and leaf-like.

questions.q: The chloroplast of Spirogyra is
questions.x: One or more spiral ribbon chloroplasts with pyrenoids give the 'water silk' its name.
questions.trap: Cup-shaped is Chlamydomonas.

questions.q: Lateral conjugation in Spirogyra takes place between
o: Adjacent cells of the same filament
questions.x: In lateral conjugation, neighbouring cells of one filament fuse through a side passage; scalariform conjugation joins two filaments.
questions.trap: Two filaments side by side is scalariform.

questions.q: The only diploid structure in the life cycle of Spirogyra is the
questions.x: The haploid filament forms a 2n zygospore after fusion; it undergoes meiosis on germination (haplontic cycle).
questions.trap: The filament is haploid, not diploid.

questions.q: The reserve food of red algae is
questions.x: Rhodophyceae store floridean starch; Phaeophyceae store laminarin and mannitol.
questions.trap: Laminarin and mannitol are brown algal stores.

questions.q: Agar used in culture media is obtained from
questions.x: Agar is a polysaccharide extracted from red algae such as Gelidium and Gracilaria.
questions.trap: Laminaria gives algin, not agar.

questions.q: Algin (alginic acid), used as a thickener in ice cream, is obtained from
questions.x: Alginates come from the walls of brown algae such as Laminaria and Macrocystis.
questions.trap: Red algae give agar and carrageenan.

questions.q: Bryophytes are called the amphibians of the plant kingdom because they
o: Live on land but need water for fertilisation
questions.x: Their flagellated sperms must swim through water to reach the archegonium.

questions.q: Mosses differ from ferns in having
o: A sporophyte dependent on the gametophyte
questions.x: In mosses the gametophyte is dominant and the sporophyte (foot, seta, capsule) stays attached; ferns have an independent vascular sporophyte.
questions.trap: Dominant sporophyte describes ferns.

questions.s: Morphological structure and reproduction of Marchantia
questions.q: Marchantia reproduces vegetatively by
questions.x: Cup-shaped gemma cups on the dorsal thallus surface bear multicellular gemmae dispersed by rain drops.

questions.s: Morphological structure and reproduction of Marchantia
questions.q: In Marchantia, the archegonia are borne on
questions.x: Marchantia is dioecious: female thalli bear umbrella-like archegoniophores, male thalli bear antheridiophores.
questions.trap: Gemma cups bear gemmae, not sex organs.

questions.q: A bryophyte whose sporophyte keeps growing from a basal intercalary meristem is
questions.x: The horn-like sporophyte of Anthoceros has a basal meristem and a central columella, giving continuous growth.
questions.trap: Funaria has a fixed foot-seta-capsule sporophyte.

questions.q: On germination, the spore of Funaria first forms a filamentous
questions.x: The green branched protonema bears buds that grow into leafy gametophores.
questions.trap: Prothallus is the fern gametophyte.

questions.q: The first vascular land plants without seeds are
questions.x: Pteridophytes (vascular cryptogams) have xylem and phloem but reproduce by spores.
questions.trap: Bryophytes lack true vascular tissue.

questions.s: Morphological structure and reproduction of Dryopteris
questions.q: In Dryopteris, each sorus is covered by a kidney-shaped
questions.x: The reniform indusium protects young sporangia; the annulus is the ring on the sporangium that aids dehiscence.
questions.trap: Annulus is on the sporangium, not over the sorus.

questions.s: Morphological structure and reproduction of Dryopteris
questions.q: The prothallus of Dryopteris is
questions.x: The heart-shaped gametophyte grows from a haploid spore and bears both antheridia and archegonia.
questions.trap: Diploid is the sporophyte.

questions.s: Morphological structure and reproduction of Dryopteris
questions.q: The stele in the rhizome of the fern Dryopteris is
questions.x: Overlapping leaf gaps break the vascular cylinder into a network of meristeles: a dictyostele.
questions.trap: Atactostele is the monocot stem stele.

questions.q: Gymnosperms are so called because their
o: Ovules are not enclosed in an ovary
questions.x: Gymnos = naked: ovules lie exposed on megasporophylls; there is no ovary or fruit.

questions.q: Edible chilgoza seeds are obtained from
questions.x: Chilgoza pine (P. gerardiana) of dry inner Himalaya yields edible seeds.
questions.trap: P. roxburghii is chir pine, tapped for resin.

questions.s: Morphological structure and reproduction of Pinus
questions.q: In Pinus roxburghii (khote salla), each dwarf shoot bears needles in groups of
questions.x: Chir pine needles occur in threes; blue pine (P. wallichiana) has five per dwarf shoot.
questions.trap: Five belongs to P. wallichiana.

questions.s: Morphological structure and reproduction of Pinus
questions.q: The pollen grain of Pinus has two wings, which help in
questions.x: The two air sacs make pollen light and buoyant for anemophily.

questions.s: Morphological structure and reproduction of Pinus
questions.q: Male and female cones of Pinus develop on the same plant. Pinus is therefore
questions.x: Monoecious plants bear both sexes on one individual; Cycas, in contrast, is dioecious.
questions.trap: Cycas is the dioecious gymnosperm.

questions.q: Turpentine is obtained from the resin of
questions.x: Distilling Pinus resin gives turpentine oil and rosin.
questions.trap: Ephedra gives the drug ephedrine.

questions.q: The drug ephedrine, used to relieve asthma, is obtained from
questions.x: Ephedrine from Ephedra dilates bronchi; Taxus yields the anticancer drug taxol.
questions.trap: Taxus gives taxol, an anticancer drug.

questions.q: Ginger is an underground stem modification called a
questions.x: Ginger grows horizontally with nodes, internodes, scale leaves and buds: a rhizome.
questions.trap: Potato is a tuber; onion a bulb.

questions.q: Banana is propagated vegetatively by
questions.x: Lateral shoots (suckers) arising from the underground stem grow into new plants.
questions.trap: Root tubers are sweet potato.

questions.q: Stilt roots of maize and sugarcane arise from
o: The pericycle of the primary root
The lower nodes of the stem
questions.x: They are adventitious roots growing obliquely from basal nodes to support the stem.
questions.trap: Radicle forms the tap root, not stilt roots.

questions.q: A potato is a modified stem, not a root, because it bears
questions.x: The eyes are nodes with buds in the axil of scale leaves, a stem feature.
questions.trap: Storing starch happens in roots too.

questions.q: The green, needle-like 'leaves' of Asparagus are actually
questions.x: Cladodes are short branches of limited growth that photosynthesise; the true leaves are scales.
questions.trap: Phyllode is a flattened petiole (Acacia).

questions.q: Pneumatophores (breathing roots) are found in
questions.x: Mangroves in waterlogged saline mud send negatively geotropic roots up for aeration.
questions.trap: Banyan has prop roots.

questions.q: A cup-like involucre containing a single central female flower surrounded by many male flowers is
questions.x: Cyathium is the inflorescence of Euphorbia (poinsettia).
questions.trap: Hypanthodium is the fig inflorescence.

questions.q: In a racemose inflorescence,
o: The main axis ends in a flower
The main axis grows indefinitely and flowers open acropetally
questions.x: Racemose: oldest flowers at the base, youngest at the tip; cymose axis ends in a flower.
questions.trap: Ending in a flower is cymose.

questions.q: Apple is called a false fruit because its edible part develops from the
questions.x: A fruit formed mainly from parts other than the ovary is false (pseudocarp); apple's fleshy part is thalamus.
questions.trap: Ovary wall forms true fruits.

questions.q: Siliqua is the characteristic fruit of
questions.x: Siliqua develops from a bicarpellary, syncarpous superior ovary with parietal placentation and a false septum.
questions.trap: Fabaceae fruit is a legume (pod).

questions.q: The ovary of mustard becomes two-chambered because of a false septum called the
questions.x: The replum grows between the two parietal placentae of the Brassicaceae ovary.
questions.trap: Raphe is the ridge of an anatropous ovule.

questions.q: Diadelphous stamens arranged as (9) + 1 are characteristic of
questions.x: In pea nine stamens are fused into a tube and the posterior one is free.
questions.trap: Brassicaceae has tetradynamous stamens.

questions.q: The floral formula ⊕ ⚥ P₃₊₃ A₃₊₃ G₍₃₎ represents the family
questions.x: Six tepals and six stamens in two whorls of three with a tricarpellary superior ovary: a trimerous monocot family (onion).
questions.trap: Solanaceae is pentamerous with G(2).

questions.q: Which plant does NOT belong to Solanaceae?
questions.x: Onion (Allium cepa) is in Liliaceae; Datura, brinjal and tomato are Solanaceae.

questions.q: Ovary of Liliaceae (e.g. onion) is
o: Tricarpellary, syncarpous, superior with axile placentation
questions.x: Liliaceae: G(3), trilocular, superior, axile placentation.
questions.trap: Bicarpellary oblique is Solanaceae.

questions.q: Sphagnum (peat moss) is used by gardeners as a packing material because it
questions.x: Its dead hyaline cells absorb many times their weight of water; it also forms peat fuel.

questions.s: Uses of medicinal plants of Nepal
questions.q: Azadirachtin, a natural insecticide, is obtained from
questions.x: Neem seeds and leaves give azadirachtin; neem is also antiseptic and used for skin disease.

questions.s: Uses of medicinal plants of Nepal
questions.q: Reserpine from the roots of Sarpagandha (Rauwolfia serpentina) is used to treat
questions.x: Reserpine lowers blood pressure and acts as a tranquiliser.
questions.trap: Malaria drug quinine comes from Cinchona.

questions.s: Uses of medicinal plants of Nepal
questions.q: Yarsagumba (Ophiocordyceps sinensis) is
o: The root of a Himalayan herb
A fungus growing on a moth caterpillar
questions.x: The fungus infects ghost-moth larvae in the soil and sends up a club-shaped fruiting body; used as a tonic.
questions.trap: Its root-like look misleads students.

questions.s: Uses of medicinal plants of Nepal
questions.q: Leaves of Tulsi (Ocimum sanctum) are traditionally used to treat
questions.x: Tulsi leaf extract is expectorant and antimicrobial, used for cough, cold and fever.

questions.s: Uses of medicinal plants of Nepal
questions.q: The rhizome of Zingiber officinale is widely used to relieve
questions.x: Gingerols in ginger are carminative and anti-emetic, easing nausea, indigestion and sore throat.
questions.trap: Blood pressure is the Sarpagandha use.

questions.q: Milk turns into curd because of the bacterium
questions.x: Lactobacillus ferments lactose to lactic acid, which coagulates milk protein.

questions.q: In a pond ecosystem, phytoplankton are
questions.x: Phytoplankton (e.g. diatoms, Volvox) photosynthesise and form the first trophic level.
questions.trap: Zooplankton are the primary consumers.

questions.q: Rooted plants with floating leaves, like the water lily (Nymphaea), grow in the pond's
questions.x: The shallow, well-lit shore region (littoral) supports rooted vegetation.
questions.trap: Limnetic is open water with plankton only.

questions.q: By the 10% law, if primary consumers of a grassland receive 2000 J, the energy fixed by producers was about
questions.x: Only ~10% passes up each level, so producers = 2000 × 10 = 20,000 J.
questions.trap: 200 J is the next level up, not down.

questions.q: Many interlinked food chains in an ecosystem together form a
questions.x: A food web gives alternative pathways, making the ecosystem more stable.

questions.q: An orchid growing on a mango branch, using it only for support, shows
questions.x: Epiphytes benefit and the tree is neither helped nor harmed (+, 0).
questions.trap: It is not a parasite: it makes its own food.

questions.q: Penicillium secreting penicillin that kills nearby bacteria is an example of
questions.x: Amensalism (−, 0): one species is harmed while the other is unaffected; also called antibiosis.

questions.q: Cuscuta (dodder) growing on other plants is a
questions.x: Leafless, yellow Cuscuta lacks chlorophyll and draws food from the host phloem by haustoria.
questions.trap: Mistletoe (Loranthus) is the partial parasite.

questions.q: Conversion of ammonia to nitrite in the soil is carried out by
questions.x: Nitrification step 1: Nitrosomonas oxidises NH₃ to NO₂⁻; step 2: Nitrobacter oxidises NO₂⁻ to NO₃⁻.
questions.trap: Nitrobacter does the second step.

questions.q: Bacteria that return nitrogen gas to the atmosphere by reducing nitrates are
questions.x: Denitrification: NO₃⁻ → N₂ under anaerobic conditions by Pseudomonas and Thiobacillus denitrificans.

questions.q: In the carbon cycle, carbon dioxide is removed from the atmosphere mainly by
questions.x: Green plants fix CO₂ into sugars; the other three release CO₂.

questions.q: The gas contributing most to the human-enhanced greenhouse effect is
questions.x: CO₂ from fossil fuels and deforestation is the largest anthropogenic contributor; methane, N₂O and CFCs follow.
questions.trap: N₂ and O₂ do not absorb infrared.

questions.q: A major agricultural source of the greenhouse gas methane is
questions.x: Anaerobic methanogens in waterlogged rice fields and cattle guts release CH₄.

questions.q: The ozone layer lies in the
questions.x: Ozone is concentrated about 15–35 km up in the stratosphere and absorbs UV-B.

questions.q: The main cause of ozone layer depletion is
questions.x: UV splits CFCs to free Cl atoms; one Cl atom can destroy thousands of O₃ molecules.
questions.trap: SO₂ causes acid rain instead.

questions.q: Thickness of the ozone layer is measured in
questions.x: 1 Dobson unit = 0.01 mm of pure ozone at STP.

questions.q: Acid rain is mainly caused by atmospheric
questions.x: SO₂ and NOₓ dissolve in rain to form H₂SO₄ and HNO₃, giving pH below 5.6.

questions.q: Sal (Shorea robusta) forests of Nepal mainly occur in the
questions.x: Sal dominates tropical deciduous forests below about 1000 m.

questions.q: Schima–Castanopsis forest (chilaune–katus) is typical of which zone of Nepal?
questions.x: Schima wallichii and Castanopsis dominate the subtropical broad-leaved belt of the mid-hills.
questions.trap: Tropical zone is Sal.

questions.q: The highest species diversity on Earth is found in
questions.x: Warm, wet, stable climate with high productivity supports maximum species richness.

questions.q: Which invasive alien plant smothers grasslands and forests of Chitwan National Park?
questions.x: Mikania, a fast-growing climber from tropical America, covers native vegetation; the others are native trees.

questions.q: Water hyacinth (Eichhornia crassipes) spreading over lakes such as Phewa is an example of
questions.x: An introduced species that spreads aggressively and harms native ecosystems is an invasive alien species.
questions.trap: Biomagnification concerns toxins, not species.

questions.q: The final, stable community at the end of succession is the
questions.x: The climax is in equilibrium with the climate and changes little thereafter.
questions.trap: Pioneers are the first colonisers.

questions.q: Succession on abandoned farmland or a burnt forest is
questions.x: Secondary succession starts where soil already exists, so it is faster than primary succession.
questions.trap: Primary succession starts on bare rock or new water.

questions.q: The correct order of stages in a hydrosere is
o: Phytoplankton → submerged → floating → reed-swamp → sedge-meadow → woodland
Phytoplankton → floating → submerged → sedge-meadow → reed-swamp → woodland
Submerged → phytoplankton → floating → reed-swamp → woodland → sedge-meadow
Phytoplankton → submerged → reed-swamp → floating → sedge-meadow → woodland
questions.x: Water gets shallower stage by stage as dead matter fills the pond, ending in forest.
questions.trap: Swapping floating and reed-swamp is the common error.

questions.q: Sunken stomata and a thick cuticle are adaptations of
questions.x: These features cut transpiration in dry habitats, e.g. Nerium.

questions.q: Well-developed aerenchyma for buoyancy and aeration is a feature of
questions.x: Air-filled spaces keep Hydrilla and lotus afloat and supply O₂ to submerged parts.

questions.q: Plants that grow best in full sunlight are called
questions.x: Helios = sun; sciophytes are shade-loving plants.
questions.trap: Sciophytes are shade lovers.

questions.q: Increase in length at the tips of root and shoot is due to
questions.x: Apical meristems at the tips cause primary growth in length; lateral meristems increase girth.

questions.q: Intercalary meristem is found
o: At the base of internodes in grasses
questions.x: It lies between permanent tissues and lets grass stems re-grow after grazing.

questions.q: Living cells with cellulose and pectin thickening at the corners, giving support to young dicot stems, are
questions.x: Collenchyma forms the hypodermis of dicot stems and gives flexible support.
questions.trap: Sclerenchyma is dead and lignified.

questions.q: Fibres and sclereids are types of
questions.x: Both are dead cells with thick lignified walls; fibres are long, sclereids short (stone cells of pear).

questions.q: The only living component of xylem is
questions.x: Xylem parenchyma stores food and helps radial conduction; tracheids, vessels and fibres are dead at maturity.
questions.trap: Vessels conduct water but are dead.

questions.q: Companion cells associated with sieve tubes are found in
questions.x: Gymnosperms and pteridophytes have albuminous cells and sieve cells instead.

questions.q: Vessels are generally absent in
questions.x: Most gymnosperm xylem has only tracheids; Gnetales are the exception with vessels.
questions.trap: Gnetum is the gymnosperm that does have vessels.

questions.q: Conjoint, collateral and open vascular bundles occur in
questions.x: Xylem and phloem lie on the same radius with cambium between them, so the bundle is open.
questions.trap: Monocot stem bundles are closed.

questions.q: Bicollateral vascular bundles, with phloem on both sides of xylem, are found in
questions.x: Cucurbitaceae stems show outer phloem, outer cambium, xylem, inner cambium, inner phloem.

questions.q: Concentric (amphicribral) bundles, in which phloem surrounds xylem, are common in
questions.x: Amphicribral (hadrocentric) bundles occur in ferns; amphivasal (xylem around phloem) in Dracaena and Yucca.
questions.trap: Dracaena has the reverse (amphivasal).

questions.q: Radial vascular bundles, with xylem and phloem on different radii, occur in
questions.x: In roots xylem and phloem strands alternate; stems and leaves have conjoint bundles.

questions.s: Study of monocot and dicot stem
questions.q: The stele of a monocot stem, with bundles scattered in ground tissue, is called
questions.x: Atacto = irregular; dicot stems have a ring of bundles (eustele).
questions.trap: Eustele is the dicot stem ring.

questions.s: Study of monocot and dicot stem
questions.q: Vascular bundles with a sclerenchymatous sheath and a lysigenous water cavity are seen in the T.S. of
questions.x: Monocot stem bundles are skull-shaped; the protoxylem breaks down to leave a water cavity.
questions.trap: Sunflower has open bundles without a cavity.

questions.s: Study of monocot and dicot root
questions.q: Polyarch xylem with a large, well-developed pith is a feature of
questions.x: Monocot roots usually have more than six xylem groups and a big pith; dicot roots are di- to tetrarch with little pith.

questions.s: Study of monocot and dicot root
questions.q: In roots, protoxylem lies towards the periphery. This condition is
questions.x: Exarch xylem matures centripetally; stems are endarch.
questions.trap: Endarch is the stem condition.

questions.s: Study of monocot and dicot root
questions.q: Lateral roots arise from the
questions.x: Lateral roots are endogenous: they originate in the pericycle opposite protoxylem and push through the cortex.
questions.trap: Endodermis lies just outside the pericycle.

questions.s: Study of monocot and dicot leaf
questions.q: Bulliform (motor) cells that help leaves roll in dry weather are found in the upper epidermis of
questions.x: Large thin-walled bulliform cells of monocot (isobilateral) leaves lose water and make the leaf curl.

questions.s: Study of monocot and dicot leaf
questions.q: A dorsiventral leaf, with mesophyll differentiated into palisade and spongy tissue, is typical of
questions.x: Palisade lies under the upper epidermis; spongy tissue with air spaces lies below. Monocot leaves are isobilateral.

questions.q: Dumb-bell-shaped guard cells are found in the stomata of
questions.x: Grass guard cells are dumb-bell shaped with subsidiary cells; dicots have kidney-shaped guard cells.
questions.trap: Kidney-shaped is the dicot type.

questions.s: Study of monocot and dicot leaf
questions.q: Kranz anatomy, in which bundle-sheath cells around veins contain large chloroplasts, is seen in leaves of
questions.x: Kranz anatomy marks C₄ plants such as maize, sugarcane and sorghum; wheat, rice and pea are C₃.
questions.trap: Wheat and rice are grasses but C₃.

questions.q: The ability of a single plant cell to regenerate a whole plant is called
questions.x: Totipotency, predicted by Haberlandt (1902), is the basis of plant tissue culture.

questions.q: The father of plant tissue culture is
questions.x: Haberlandt (1902) first tried culturing isolated plant cells; Steward later raised carrot plants from single cells.
questions.trap: Paul Berg is linked to recombinant DNA.

questions.q: Before inoculation, explants are surface-sterilised using
o: Sodium hypochlorite or mercuric chloride solution
Dry heat in an oven at 160 °C
questions.x: Living explants are dipped in disinfectant (NaOCl, HgCl₂, 70% ethanol) then rinsed; heat would kill them.
questions.trap: Autoclaving is for media and glassware, not tissue.

questions.q: Culture media in tissue culture are sterilised by autoclaving at
questions.x: Moist heat under pressure kills spores; −196 °C is cryopreservation.

questions.q: An unorganised, undifferentiated mass of cells formed in tissue culture is
questions.x: Callus forms when auxin and cytokinin are balanced; it can later redifferentiate.
questions.trap: Explant is the starting piece of tissue.

questions.q: Haploid plants are raised in tissue culture from
questions.x: Pollen is haploid, so anther culture gives haploids that can be doubled to homozygous lines.
questions.trap: Endosperm culture gives triploids.

questions.q: The 'pomato' was produced by
questions.x: Protoplasts are freed by cellulase and pectinase, fused with PEG, and grown into a somatic hybrid.
questions.trap: Grafting does not combine genomes.

questions.q: Plants produced by micropropagation from one parent are
questions.x: Mitotic multiplication of explants gives true-to-type clones (somaclones), useful for banana, orchids, potato.

questions.q: For long-term germplasm storage, cells and embryos are cryopreserved in liquid nitrogen at
questions.x: Liquid nitrogen boils at −196 °C, halting all metabolism so tissue can be stored indefinitely.
questions.trap: −80 °C is a deep freezer, not liquid nitrogen.

questions.q: The enzyme that joins DNA fragments in recombinant DNA technology is
questions.x: Ligase (molecular glue) seals phosphodiester bonds; restriction enzymes (molecular scissors) cut.
questions.trap: Restriction enzymes cut, they do not join.

questions.q: Bt cotton resists bollworm because it carries the cry gene from
questions.x: Cry genes code for Bt toxin, which kills the larvae when they eat the plant.
questions.trap: Agrobacterium is the vector, not the toxin source.

questions.q: Golden rice is genetically engineered to contain
questions.x: It fights vitamin A deficiency; its yellow colour comes from β-carotene.

questions.q: The heat-stable DNA polymerase used in PCR is obtained from
questions.x: Taq polymerase survives the 94 °C denaturation step of each PCR cycle.

questions.q: During agarose gel electrophoresis, DNA fragments move towards the
o: Anode, because DNA is negatively charged
questions.x: Phosphate groups make DNA negative, so it migrates to the positive electrode; smaller fragments move farther.

questions.q: A biofertilizer that fixes nitrogen in the root nodules of legumes is
questions.x: Rhizobium lives symbiotically in nodules; Azotobacter is free-living.
questions.trap: Azotobacter fixes N₂ but freely in soil.

questions.q: Azolla is used as a biofertilizer in paddy fields because it harbours the nitrogen-fixing cyanobacterium
questions.x: Anabaena lives in leaf cavities of the water fern Azolla and fixes nitrogen for rice.

questions.q: Green manuring means
o: Ploughing a young leguminous crop into the soil
questions.x: A crop such as Sesbania or sunn hemp is buried before flowering; it adds organic matter and nitrogen.
questions.trap: Cattle dung is farmyard manure.

questions.q: The superiority of a hybrid over both its parents is called
questions.x: Heterosis (hybrid vigour) is exploited in hybrid maize and rice.
questions.trap: Inbreeding depression is the opposite.

questions.q: The Green Revolution, based on semi-dwarf high-yielding wheat, is associated with
questions.x: Borlaug developed semi-dwarf, disease-resistant wheat varieties (Nobel Peace Prize 1970).

questions.q: In Nepal, bio-engineering on roadside slopes means
o: Using live plants such as grasses and bamboo to stabilise slopes
questions.x: Roots bind soil and vegetation reduces surface erosion and shallow landslides, often combined with small structures.
questions.trap: Gene insertion is genetic engineering.

questions.q: Aflatoxin, a cancer-causing contaminant of stored maize and groundnut, is produced by
questions.x: Damp storage lets A. flavus grow and secrete aflatoxin, a liver carcinogen; proper drying prevents it.

questions.q: Food security exists when
o: A country exports most of its grain
Food is stored in government warehouses
All people at all times have access to sufficient, safe and nutritious food
questions.x: FAO definition: availability, access, utilisation and stability of safe, nutritious food for everyone.

questions.q: In old or dormant sieve tubes, the sieve pores become plugged by a deposit of
questions.x: Callose, a β-1,3-glucan, forms pads on sieve plates of dormant or ageing sieve tubes and blocks translocation.
questions.trap: Tyloses plug old xylem vessels, not sieve tubes.

questions.q: Sclerenchyma fibres are long, pointed cells with
o: Thin cellulose walls and a large central vacuole
Corner thickenings of pectin and a living protoplast
Thick lignified walls and a very narrow lumen
questions.x: Fibres are dead at maturity; heavy lignin deposition leaves only a narrow lumen, giving mechanical strength (jute, hemp).
questions.trap: Corner thickening describes collenchyma.

questions.q: An interaction in which both species benefit and neither can survive without the other is
questions.x: Mutualism (+,+) is obligatory, e.g. the alga and fungus of a lichen; protocooperation is also (+,+) but optional, e.g. sea anemone and hermit crab.
questions.trap: Protocooperation also benefits both, but the partners can live apart.

questions.q: Organisms that live on or in the bottom sediments of a sea or lake are called
questions.x: Benthos live on the bottom; plankton drift with currents; nekton swim actively (fish); neuston live at the surface film.

questions.q: Velamen, a spongy tissue that absorbs moisture from humid air, covers the aerial roots of
questions.x: Epiphytic orchids such as Vanda hang aerial roots whose dead, spongy velamen soaks up rain and moist air.
questions.trap: Rhizophora has pneumatophores, not velamen.

questions.q: Grafting is generally not successful in monocots because they
questions.x: A graft unites when the cambia of stock and scion join and form new tissue; monocot bundles are closed (no cambium), so no union forms.
questions.trap: Scattered bundles are true of monocots, but the missing cambium is the reason.

questions.q: Fertiliser runoff rich in nitrate and phosphate causes algal blooms in a pond and a fall in its dissolved oxygen. This process is
questions.x: Nutrient enrichment → algal bloom → dead algae decomposed by aerobic bacteria → dissolved O₂ falls and fish die.
questions.trap: Biomagnification is the build-up of toxins like DDT along food chains.

questions.q: On germination, the zygospore of Spirogyra first undergoes
o: Meiosis, so the new filament is haploid
Mitosis, so the new filament is diploid
questions.x: The zygospore is the only diploid cell; it divides by meiosis (zygotic meiosis), three nuclei degenerate and the surviving haploid cell grows into a filament.
questions.trap: Spirogyra filaments are haploid, so a diploid filament never forms.

questions.q: Four free petals, each narrowed into a claw and a spreading limb and arranged like a cross, are characteristic of
questions.x: The mustard family has a cruciform corolla: four clawed petals in a cross, hence the old name Cruciferae.
questions.trap: Fabaceae petals are unequal (standard, wings, keel), not cruciform.

questions.q: Red algae can grow at greater depths in the sea than other algae because
o: They lack chlorophyll and do not need light
Phycoerythrin absorbs the blue-green light that reaches deep water
Fucoxanthin absorbs the red light found at depth
They obtain food as parasites of corals
questions.x: Red light is absorbed near the surface; phycoerythrin captures the blue-green light that penetrates deep, so red algae live deepest.
questions.trap: Fucoxanthin is the brown-algal pigment.

questions.q: Which of these cells is living at functional maturity?
questions.x: Companion cells keep a nucleus and dense cytoplasm and support the enucleate sieve tube; vessels, tracheids and cork cells are dead.

questions.q: Flattened green stems (phylloclades) that photosynthesise while the leaves are reduced to spines, as in Opuntia, are an adaptation of
questions.x: Reducing leaves cuts water loss by transpiration; the green phylloclade or cladode takes over photosynthesis in dry habitats.

questions.q: In the sexual cycle of fungi, the correct sequence of events is
questions.x: Cytoplasms fuse first (plasmogamy), then nuclei fuse (karyogamy) to give a diploid zygote nucleus, which undergoes meiosis to form haploid spores.

questions.q: A food chain that begins with living green plants eaten by herbivores is a
questions.x: Grazing chains start with producers (grass → grasshopper → frog → snake → hawk); detritus chains start with dead organic matter.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a trophic level?
questions.x: A trophic level is one feeding step (producer, herbivore, carnivore). A food web is the whole network of interlinked chains, not a step.

questions.q: The antherozoids of a fern such as Dryopteris are
questions.x: Fern antherozoids are coiled with many flagella and swim through water to the archegonium; moss antherozoids are biflagellate.
questions.trap: Biflagellate antherozoids belong to mosses.

questions.q: Cork (phellem) cells are impermeable to water and gases because their walls are impregnated with
questions.x: Suberin, a waxy fatty substance, makes cork cells dead and impervious, so bark protects the stem; it also suits bottle stoppers.
questions.trap: Lignin hardens xylem and sclerenchyma walls.

questions.q: Two species with exactly the same niche cannot coexist indefinitely. This is
questions.x: Gause's Paramecium experiments showed the better competitor eliminates the other when their niches fully overlap.

questions.q: Plants that reproduce by spores and never form seeds are grouped as
questions.x: Cryptogams (algae, bryophytes, pteridophytes) have hidden reproduction and no seeds; phanerogams (gymnosperms and angiosperms) bear seeds.

questions.q: Conversion of the organic nitrogen of dead plants and animals into ammonia by decomposers is
questions.x: Decomposer bacteria and fungi break proteins and urea down to NH₃; nitrifying bacteria then oxidise NH₃ to nitrite and nitrate.
questions.trap: Nitrification starts from ammonia; it does not produce it.

questions.q: Iodine is commercially extracted from
questions.x: Large brown seaweeds such as Laminaria concentrate iodine from sea water; kelp ash was long the main source of iodine.
questions.trap: Gelidium gives agar, not iodine.

questions.q: The rhizoids of a liverwort such as Marchantia are
questions.x: Liverworts have unicellular rhizoids (smooth-walled and tuberculate); mosses such as Funaria have multicellular rhizoids with oblique septa.
questions.trap: Multicellular rhizoids belong to mosses.

questions.q: Hygroscopic elaters that help in spore dispersal are found in the capsule of
questions.x: The sporophyte capsule of Marchantia contains spores mixed with diploid elaters having spiral thickenings; they twist with changes in humidity and scatter spores.
questions.trap: Funaria uses peristome teeth, not elaters.

questions.q: In the capsule of Funaria, the gradual release of spores in dry weather is controlled by hygroscopic
questions.x: The peristome is a ring of teeth around the capsule mouth; the teeth bend in and out with humidity, letting spores out only in dry air.
questions.trap: Elaters belong to liverworts like Marchantia.

questions.q: Mucilage cavities in the thallus of the hornwort Anthoceros usually contain colonies of
questions.x: Anthoceros houses the nitrogen-fixing cyanobacterium Nostoc in mucilage-filled cavities on the lower side of its thallus.
questions.trap: Anabaena lives in the water fern Azolla.

questions.q: Both chlorophyll a and chlorophyll b are present in
questions.x: Green algae share chlorophyll a and b with land plants; brown algae have a and c, red algae a and d, and cyanobacteria only a.

questions.q: Chlamydomonas is an example of a
questions.x: Chlamydomonas is a single biflagellate green cell with a cup-shaped chloroplast; Volvox is colonial and Spirogyra filamentous.
questions.trap: Volvox is the colonial one.

questions.q: The motile zoospores and gametes of brown algae bear
o: Two equal flagella attached at the apex
questions.x: Phaeophyceae have pear-shaped motile cells with two unequal, laterally inserted flagella; green algae have 2–8 equal apical flagella.
questions.trap: Equal apical flagella describe green algae.

questions.q: Which algal class has no flagellated cells at any stage of its life cycle?
questions.x: Red algae have non-motile spores and gametes; the male gamete (spermatium) is carried passively by water currents.

questions.q: The mycelium of Phycomycetes such as Mucor and Rhizopus is
o: Absent, as the fungus is unicellular
questions.x: Phycomycetes have tubular hyphae without cross walls, so many nuclei share one cytoplasm (coenocytic). Septate hyphae occur in higher fungi.
questions.trap: Dikaryotic septate hyphae belong to Basidiomycetes.

questions.q: In an ascus of Neurospora, the diploid nucleus undergoes meiosis followed by one mitosis. The number of ascospores formed is
questions.x: Meiosis gives 4 haploid nuclei; one mitosis doubles them to 8, each becoming an ascospore arranged in a row inside the ascus.
questions.trap: 4 stops after meiosis and ignores the mitosis.

questions.q: The common edible mushroom Agaricus belongs to
questions.x: Agaricus forms basidiospores on basidia lining the gills of its fruiting body, so it is a basidiomycete.
questions.trap: Morels and yeast are the edible ascomycetes.

questions.q: Alternaria and Colletotrichum, which cause leaf-spot and anthracnose diseases of crops, belong to
questions.x: Both reproduce only by conidia; no sexual stage is known, so they are placed in Deuteromycetes (fungi imperfecti).

questions.q: Mucor reproduces asexually by
o: Conidia cut off at hyphal tips
questions.x: A sporangiophore of Mucor ends in a round sporangium with a columella; it releases many non-motile sporangiospores that grow into new mycelia.
questions.trap: Conidia are the asexual spores of Penicillium and Aspergillus.

questions.q: Sexual reproduction in yeast produces
questions.x: Two haploid cells fuse; the diploid cell becomes an ascus and forms ascospores by meiosis, so yeast is an ascomycete.
questions.trap: Zygospores belong to Mucor and Rhizopus.

questions.s: Characteristics, structure, chemical composition of viruses
questions.q: The genetic material of most plant viruses is
questions.x: Most plant viruses (e.g. TMV) carry ssRNA; bacteriophages usually carry dsDNA. A virus never carries both DNA and RNA.
questions.trap: dsDNA is typical of bacteriophages like T4.

questions.q: Bacteriophages can be used beneficially to
questions.x: Phages infect and lyse specific bacteria, so they can be used to destroy pathogenic or antibiotic-resistant bacteria.

questions.q: Infoldings of the bacterial plasma membrane that help in respiration and cell-wall formation are
questions.x: Mesosomes are membrane infoldings that increase surface area for respiratory enzymes and help in DNA replication and septum formation.
questions.trap: Cristae are infoldings of mitochondria, which bacteria lack.

questions.q: Bacteria with flagella all over the cell surface, such as E. coli and Salmonella, are
questions.x: Peritrichous = flagella all around; monotrichous = one; lophotrichous = a tuft at one end; amphitrichous = at both ends.

questions.q: Purple sulphur bacteria make food using light energy and H₂S as the hydrogen donor. Their mode of nutrition is
questions.x: Light is the energy source, so they are photoautotrophs; H₂S only replaces water as the electron donor, so no oxygen is released.
questions.trap: H₂S suggests chemoautotrophy, but energy comes from light.

questions.q: The antibiotic streptomycin is obtained from
questions.x: Streptomycin, used against tuberculosis, was isolated by Waksman from the filamentous bacterium (actinomycete) Streptomyces griseus.
questions.trap: Penicillium gives penicillin.

questions.q: Which cyanobacterium is grown as a protein-rich food supplement?
questions.x: Spirulina is cultivated as single-cell protein, being rich in protein, vitamins and minerals. Microcystis forms toxic water blooms.

questions.q: Much of the world's coal was formed from the buried remains of ancient
o: Pteridophytes such as giant club mosses and horsetails
questions.x: Tree-sized lycopods (Lepidodendron) and horsetails (Calamites) of the Carboniferous swamp forests were buried and compressed into coal.

questions.q: In pteridophytes, the dominant and independent plant body is the
questions.x: The fern plant with roots, stem and leaves is the sporophyte; the gametophyte is a small, short-lived prothallus.
questions.trap: The haploid gametophyte dominates in bryophytes, not ferns.

questions.q: Which of the following is absent in gymnosperms?
o: Triple fusion forming a triploid endosperm
questions.x: Gymnosperms bear naked ovules that become seeds and shed pollen, but their endosperm is the haploid female gametophyte formed before fertilisation, so triple fusion never occurs.
questions.trap: Naked seeds are the hallmark of gymnosperms.

questions.s: Morphological structure and reproduction of Pinus
questions.q: The male gametes of Pinus are
o: Non-motile and carried to the egg by a pollen tube
Multiflagellate and swim to the egg
Biflagellate and swim to the egg
Absent, as Pinus reproduces only vegetatively
questions.x: Pinus shows siphonogamy: the pollen tube delivers non-motile male gametes to the archegonium, so no water is needed.
questions.trap: Cycas has motile multiflagellate sperms; Pinus does not.

questions.q: Monocots usually have parallel venation. Which monocot is an exception with reticulate venation?
questions.x: Smilax (and Dioscorea) are monocots with net-like venation; banana has pinnate parallel venation and maize and onion have parallel venation.
questions.trap: Banana leaves look net-like but are parallel-veined.

questions.q: In garden pea, the terminal leaflets of the compound leaf are modified into
questions.x: Pea climbs using leaflet tendrils; its large leafy stipules take over much of the photosynthesis.

questions.q: In Australian Acacia, the flattened green petiole that does the work of the lamina is a
questions.x: A phyllode is a leaf-like petiole; the true leaflets fall early. Phylloclades and cladodes are modified stems.
questions.trap: Phylloclade sounds similar but is a stem.

questions.q: The inflorescence of sunflower is a
questions.x: In a capitulum, many sessile florets (ray and disc) sit on a flattened receptacle surrounded by involucral bracts.

questions.q: A flower in which sepals, petals and stamens arise below the ovary is
questions.x: When the ovary sits highest on the thalamus and other parts arise beneath it, the flower is hypogynous and the ovary superior (e.g. mustard, brinjal).
questions.trap: Epigynous flowers have inferior ovaries, with parts above them.

questions.q: Stamens united by their anthers but with free filaments, as in sunflower, are
questions.x: Syngenesious stamens form an anther tube around the style (Asteraceae). Adelphous terms refer to fused filaments.
questions.trap: Monadelphous means filaments fused, as in China rose.

questions.q: Which of the following is an aggregate fruit?
questions.x: An aggregate fruit develops from the free carpels of one flower (custard apple, strawberry). Mulberry and pineapple are multiple fruits from whole inflorescences; mango is simple.
questions.trap: Pineapple and mulberry come from many flowers: multiple fruits.

questions.q: The floral formula ⊕ ⚥ K₍₅₎ C₍₅₎ A₅ G₍₂₎ (stamens epipetalous) belongs to
questions.x: Five united sepals and petals, five epipetalous stamens and a bicarpellary syncarpous ovary fit Solanaceae. Brassicaceae has K₂₊₂ C₄ A₂₊₄; Liliaceae P₃₊₃.

questions.q: The characteristic fruit of Fabaceae is a
questions.x: A legume develops from a monocarpellary ovary and splits along both sutures. Siliqua is the mustard fruit; berry is typical of Solanaceae.

questions.q: The edible part of the onion bulb is mainly its
questions.x: An onion bulb is a reduced disc-like stem bearing fleshy scale leaves that store food; adventitious roots arise below the disc.
questions.trap: The stem is only the small basal disc.

questions.s: Economic importance of angiosperms of Nepal
questions.q: Traditional Nepali lokta paper is made from the bark fibres of
questions.x: Lokta paper is handmade from the inner bark of Daphne bholua and D. papyracea, shrubs of Nepal's mid-hills.

questions.q: In log phase, a culture grows from 1 × 10³ to 1.6 × 10⁴ cells in 2 hours. The generation time is
questions.x: Increase = 16 = 2⁴, so 4 generations in 120 min; generation time = 120/4 = 30 min.
questions.trap: Count generations (2⁴ = 16 gives 4), not the 16-fold increase.

questions.q: Members of which taxonomic category share the greatest number of common characters?
questions.x: Moving down the hierarchy from kingdom to species, groups get smaller and members share more characters; species members share the most.
questions.trap: Kingdom is the largest, broadest group.

questions.q: In Whittaker's five-kingdom system, all unicellular eukaryotes are placed in
questions.x: Monera holds prokaryotes; Protista holds unicellular eukaryotes such as Chlamydomonas, Euglena, diatoms and Amoeba.
questions.trap: Monera contains only prokaryotes.

questions.q: In a lichen, the algal partner is the phycobiont and the fungal partner is the
questions.x: The fungus (mycobiont) gives shelter, water and minerals; the alga (phycobiont) makes food by photosynthesis.

questions.q: Vertical layering of a forest into canopy, shrub, herb and ground layers is called
questions.x: Stratification is the vertical arrangement of plants of different heights; it lets each layer use a different light level.

questions.q: In a pond, the pyramid of biomass is usually inverted because
o: Energy increases at higher trophic levels
Short-lived phytoplankton have less standing biomass than the consumers feeding on them
questions.x: Phytoplankton multiply fast but live briefly, so at any moment their biomass is smaller than that of zooplankton and fish; energy flow still decreases upward.
questions.trap: Energy never increases upward; the energy pyramid stays upright.

questions.q: The deep bottom zone of a pond, where light does not reach and photosynthesis does not occur, is the
questions.x: Littoral is the shallow edge, limnetic the open lit water, and profundal the deep dark zone where only consumers and decomposers live.
questions.trap: Limnetic is open water but still lit.

questions.q: In a pond ecosystem, the primary consumers are mainly
questions.x: Zooplankton (e.g. rotifers, crustaceans) feed directly on phytoplankton, the producers, so they are primary consumers.
questions.trap: Phytoplankton are producers.

questions.q: Rhizobium living in the root nodules of legumes shows
questions.x: Rhizobium fixes nitrogen for the plant and gets food and shelter from it: both partners benefit (+,+).

questions.q: Carbon that stays out of the active carbon cycle for millions of years is stored mainly in
questions.x: Coal, petroleum and limestone lock carbon away for geological time; burning fossil fuels returns it rapidly to the air.

questions.q: Biological nitrogen fixation converts atmospheric N₂ first into
questions.x: The enzyme nitrogenase reduces N₂ to NH₃; nitrifying bacteria later oxidise ammonia to nitrite and nitrate.
questions.trap: Nitrate is formed later by nitrification.

questions.q: A major effect of global warming in Nepal is
o: Faster melting of Himalayan glaciers and risk of glacial lake outburst floods
questions.x: Warming retreats glaciers, swells glacial lakes such as Tsho Rolpa and raises the risk of outburst floods downstream.

questions.q: Molecule for molecule, which of these greenhouse gases has the highest global-warming potential?
questions.x: CFCs trap thousands of times more heat per molecule than CO₂; CO₂ contributes most overall only because it is far more abundant.
questions.trap: CO₂ contributes most in total, not per molecule.

questions.q: Rain is called acid rain when its pH falls below about
questions.x: Normal rain is slightly acidic (pH ≈ 5.6) from dissolved CO₂; SO₂ and NOₓ forming H₂SO₄ and HNO₃ push it lower.
questions.trap: pH 7 is neutral, but clean rain is already about 5.6.

questions.q: Thinning of the ozone layer mainly increases the amount of which radiation reaching the Earth?
questions.x: Stratospheric ozone absorbs UV-B; when it thins, more UV-B reaches the ground and damages DNA, eyes and skin.
questions.trap: Infrared is linked to the greenhouse effect, not ozone.

questions.q: Forests of Rhododendron and oak (Quercus) are typical of which zone of Nepal?
questions.x: Temperate mid-mountain forests are dominated by oak, rhododendron, maple and blue pine; Sal is tropical and Schima–Castanopsis subtropical.

questions.q: Above the tree line in the Nepal Himalaya, vegetation is mainly
questions.x: Above about 4000 m, trees give way to dwarf rhododendron and juniper scrub and grassy alpine meadows.

questions.q: In a hydrosere, the stage that immediately follows the rooted floating stage (Nymphaea, Trapa) is the
questions.x: Order: phytoplankton → submerged → rooted floating → reed-swamp → sedge-meadow → woodland → climax forest.
questions.trap: Submerged comes before, not after, the floating stage.

questions.q: In a xerosere on bare rock, the community that directly replaces the crustose lichens is
questions.x: Rock xerosere: crustose lichens → foliose lichens → mosses → herbs → shrubs → climax forest; each stage adds soil for the next.
questions.trap: Mosses come after the foliose lichens.
